entities.name: HGNC:11842
observations: TLK2 amplification or overexpression was reported to impair DNA-damage checkpoint signaling in human breast-cancer models.
TLK2 regulates recovery from DNA-damage-induced G2 arrest through ASF1A-dependent chromatin restoration and pro-mitotic gene competence.

entities.name: PMID:27489360
observations: In human breast-cancer models, TLK2 amplification/overexpression impaired Chk1/Chk2-mediated DNA-damage signaling, produced a G2/M checkpoint defect, delayed DNA repair, and increased chromosomal instability.
In TCGA breast tumors, TLK2 expression correlated with genome-wide copy-number alteration burden (Spearman R=0.393, P<0.001); this tumor result is correlative.

entities.name: TLK2 amplification-CIN
observations: TLK2 amplification or overexpression can promote genomic instability by weakening the DNA-damage-induced G2/M checkpoint in breast-cancer cell models.
The conclusion is strong in the studied breast-cancer context but not established as a universal pan-cancer mechanism.
